Oral Order 04 / Dated : 09.11.2023
1.

The instant criminal misc. petition has been filed for quashing the order dated 06.01.2018 passed in Cr. Revision No. 27 of 2016, whereby and where under, the criminal revision preferred against the order dated 05.02.2015 passed by S.D.J.M., Jamshedpur in G.R. No. 70 of 2008 (Jugsalai (Bagbera)
P.S. Case No. 03 of 2008 under Sections 498A, 405, 406, 34 of the I.P.C. was allowed and the matter was remanded before the trial Court for passing order afresh on the petition which was earlier rejected under Section 319 Cr.P.C.
2.

Initially Jugsalai Bagbera P.S. Case No. 3 of 2008 was registered under Sections 498A, 405, 406,
34 of the I.P.C. on the basis of the complaint petition filed by Smt. Rajni Devi @ Babita against all together five accused persons including both these petitioners.
3. The police after investigation submitted charge-sheet against three accused persons and these petitioners were not sent up for trial.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel on behalf of the petitioners that it is a belated attempt on the part of the informant to implicate the present petitioners in the present case at the fag end of trial.

It is settled law on the point that once an accused has been discharged of the offence, he cannot be proceeded against by invoking power under Section 319 Cr.P.C.
5.

Learned counsel for opposite party No.2 submits that the trial Court has rejected the petition under Section 319 Cr.P.C on the ground of contradiction appearing in the testimony of the witnesses regarding which Revisional Court observed that the contradiction cannot be looked into at the stage while considering the petition under Section 319 Cr.P.C.
There is strong evidence regarding complicity of the petitioners in the alleged offence.
6. In order to proceed under section 319 of the Cr.P.C., it is necessary that the person should not have been shown mentioned as an accused.
The power conferred on the Court is extraordinary which is to be exercised for compelling revisions.
In the present case petitioners are uncle-in-law and aunt-in-law were named in the FIR but not sent for trial.
The trial is at its fag end.
Under the circumstance this Court is of the view that exercise of power under Section 319, for summoning the petitioners as an accused is not proper and is accordingly set aside.
Under the circumstance, the order dated 06.01.2018 passed in Cr. Revision No. 27 of 2016 is quashed so far as the petitioners, above named, are concerned.
Instant Cr. Misc. Petition is allowed.
